summary: px8my abuses npm+jsDelivr as a mutable browser-redirect channel to third-party landing pages
details: px8my ships a single browser-only script px.js which, when loaded in a web page (via jsDelivr's npm CDN), injects a full-viewport iframe (width:100vw;height:100vh;z-index:2147483647) pointing at https://mfmz.emxkm.cn/H.html?c=0gjr, covering the host page. The tarball also contains update_px8my.sh, a maintainer helper that takes a new destination domain as an argument, rewrites the hardcoded URL in px.js, increments the patch version, runs `npm publish`, and then calls the jsDelivr purge API (https://purge.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js) to flush caches — using npm+jsDelivr as rotating redirect infrastructure to attacker-selected landing pages. A comment in the script notes that curl requests are blocked by an anti-abuse control ("curl 被 tirith 拦截"), so urllib is used instead. The package has no npm lifecycle scripts and requires document/window, so `npm install px8my` and Node `require()` do not execute the redirect on the installer's machine; the harm is to browser end-users of any site that pulls px.js through the CDN.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
